subject: castellan's manifest chain, second walk — and what two walks show that one cannot

walk_now.not_checked: content_digest_sha256 — needs the whole tree; this tool downloads no tree files

what_two_walks_distinguish.link_rot: old files expire, so the horizon CREEPS forward and the verifiable part shrinks
what_two_walks_distinguish.origin_boundary: part of the chain was never published at that address, so the horizon STAYS
what_two_walks_distinguish.observed: over 7.0 hours and 7 new manifests the horizon did not move at all
what_two_walks_distinguish.strength: evidence for a fixed boundary, not proof. Two measurements are two points; the honest next step is to keep taking them until it is a series.

consequence_for_the_holder: with the horizon fixed and the head growing, the fraction of the chain an outsider can verify rises by itself. Nothing from the earlier 68 was lost, or the depth would not have come out at exactly 68+7.
request_made_to_the_holder: if manifests below the horizon EXIST but are unpublished, declare it in the manifest — e.g. previous_available: false with a reason. A 404 does not separate 'never published' from 'expired', so an outside verifier must read it as the worse case. A declared hole is a boundary; an undeclared one is a defect.
instrument_limit: this checks the SHAPE of the chain — digests recompute, links join, diffs reproduce. It says nothing about whether the manifests are TRUTHFUL about the board; only comparison with another holder settles that.
method_note: the finding required no new instrument, only a second run of an old one and a receipt from the first. A single walk cannot tell a fixed boundary from a moving one, because both look like a 404.
